note: Seed for the Joplin Data API local mock: 18 operations over note, folder and tag. Field names, nesting and types come from the OpenAPI definition and the generated client only - nothing here is copied from a live Joplin instance, though the shapes match what the Clipper Server emits.
quirks: apikey is the credential the mock accepts. The SDK sends it as a RAW `Authorization: <apikey>` header - NOT the ?token= query parameter the definition declares (PrepareAuthUtility hardcodes the header and the generator drops in/name). ?token= is accepted too, because a caller can smuggle it through the match object or direct({query}).

config.pageSize is deliberately 2 against 5 notes, so listNotes/listFolders/listTags really paginate: pages 1 and 2 answer has_more:true plus the X-Next-Page and Link rel="next" headers - which is what the paging feature reads, since NO generated target reads has_more.
config.camelHasMore adds body `hasMore` (the camelCase key PagingFeature.PreResult actually looks for). Off by default so the body stays exactly as the definition declares it.
Projects is nested inside Work (parent_id set), so listFolderNotes has a non-trivial case.
note<->tag links feed listNoteTags and listTagNotes - the two routes the SDK can only reach with a dummy `field` present and a leaked %24action query key.
Titles carry commas and colons ("Book: Designing Data-Intensive Applications", tag "reading, later") so percent-encoding on the wire is exercised.
One note is a todo with an integer todo_due, and one carries float latitude/longitude/altitude beside the integer *_time fields, so response type checking (validateContract) is meaningful.
